photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of the Caughnawaga (Kahnawake) Mohawk lacrosse team, thirteen men in period dress holding their lacrosse sticks — a documentary photo of Mohawk people and their traditional sport/equipment.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a St Regis (Akwesasne) Mohawk lacrosse team, each man holding a lacrosse stick with lacrosse balls visible in the foreground—documentary photo of Mohawk daily/cultural life directly matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The postcard shows a named Mohawk chief in full regalia (feather headdress, beaded bandolier bag, tunic, fringed leggings) photographed at Kahnawake, a Mohawk community, so it documents Mohawk dress and craft.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio-style outdoor portrait of two Kahnawake Mohawk men in feather headdresses, beaded hide shirts, and a beaded collar, identified by name — a documentary photo of Mohawk dress, matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A Mohawk man in traditional dress sits at a trade goods stall at Kahnawake (Caughnawaga), Quebec, surrounded by beadwork, baskets, and other craft items for sale — a documentary photo of Mohawk daily life and craft trade.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The postcard shows a man in feathered headdress, beaded regalia, tunic and leggings posed outdoors in Quebec, captioned "Type of Iroquois Indian of the Province of Quebec" — a documentary studio-style photo consistent with Mohawk (Iroquois) regalia and dress, though the feather headdress style is a generic "Plains-style" showpiece often adopted for photographic purposes rather than distinctly Iroquois.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The photo shows a woman in Mohawk-style fringed dress, headband with feather, and necklace, posing at a shrine in Kahnawake (Caughnawaga), a Mohawk community in Quebec — documentary dress photo consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white with colour); photographic print
photo.reason: The postcard shows a Mohawk (Iroquois) man from Caughnawaga (Kahnawake), Quebec, posed in regalia with a bow and arrow, documenting Mohawk dress and material culture.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio postcard portrait of Go-Won-Go Mohawk, a Native American (Mohawk-identified) performer, shown wearing a beaded headband, feathered ornament, and beaded/quilled jacket typical of Wild West-show "Indian" stage costume; this is a documentary photograph of a Mohawk person in decorated dress, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

household.name: Cradleboard
household.title: Cradleboard
household.reason: The image shows a painted wooden cradleboard with floral rosette designs typical of Mohawk/Haudenosaunee craft, consistent with the claimed ethnicity and category.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A woven splint bark carrying basket, a well-documented Mohawk/Iroquois craft tradition, matching the museum's attribution.

household.name: baby-carrier
household.title: baby-carrier
household.reason: The image shows a traditional wooden cradleboard/baby-carrier with carved and painted zoomorphic and floral designs, a well-documented Iroquois/Mohawk craft object attributed by the museum to the Mohawk maker.

household.name: lacrosse-stick
household.title: lacrosse-stick
household.reason: A wooden lacrosse stick with leather-thong netting, a game and object type traditionally made by the Mohawk/Iroquois, directly attributed to them by the museum.

household.name: smoking-pipe
household.title: smoking-pipe
household.reason: The object is a carved stone effigy pipe-bowl, a form well documented among Iroquois/Mohawk peoples of the Northeast, matching both the claimed ethnicity and museum attribution.

household.name: walking-stick
household.title: walking-stick
household.reason: A carved wooden walking stick with ball-in-cage openwork carving, a style well-documented among Haudenosaunee (Iroquois/Mohawk) carvers as tourist/craft trade items in the 19th–20th centuries. It's a genuine object made and used by the claimed people.

household.name: frame
household.title: frame
household.reason: This is a beaded felt "whimsy" picture frame, a well-known Iroquois/Mohawk souvenir craft tradition (whimsies made for the Niagara Falls tourist trade), attributed by the museum directly to Mohawk/Iroquois makers, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

household.name: pin cushion
household.title: pin cushion
household.reason: A beaded velvet pin cushion labeled "KANAWAKE 1946" — Kahnawake is a Mohawk reserve, and beaded souvenir pincushions were a well-known Haudenosaunee/Mohawk craft product; museum credits Mohawk/Iroquois maker.

household.name: purse; model
household.title: purse; model
household.reason: A miniature beaded felt "whimsie" purse, a well-known Iroquois/Mohawk souvenir beadwork form made for the tourist trade; this is a household/craft item made by the claimed people, not architectural sculpture as filed.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A plaited black ash splint basket attributed by the museum to the Mohawk (Iroquois), a well-known traditional craft form for this people.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A "fancy basket" made from black ash splints and sweetgrass with curled decorative elements is a well-documented Haudenosaunee/Mohawk (Akwesasne) craft tradition, and the museum explicitly attributes it to Mohawk (Akwesasne) makers.

household.name: baby-carrier; model
household.title: baby-carrier; model
household.reason: The image shows a miniature wooden cradleboard with painted triangle motifs and carved straps, explicitly attributed by the museum to the Mohawk/Iroquois, a traditional household item used for carrying infants.

household.name: bag; model
household.title: bag; model
household.reason: This is a miniature beaded "whimsy" bag made of red felt with white/green floral glass beadwork and beaded fringe, a well-documented Iroquois (including Mohawk) souvenir craft form; category should be household/beadwork, not sculpture.

instruments.name: smoking-pipe
instruments.title: smoking-pipe
instruments.reason: The image shows a carved grey stone pipe-bowl fragment with fluted decoration, attributed by the museum to Iroquois/Mohawk Northeast Peoples makers, consistent with Haudenosaunee stone pipe traditions.

garment.name: moccasin
garment.title: moccasin
garment.reason: A pair of beaded velvet-and-hide moccasins, a classic Haudenosaunee (Iroquois/Mohawk) craft form using floral beadwork typical of Northeast Woodlands peoples; the museum directly attributes it to Mohawk/Iroquois makers.

garment.name: moccasin
garment.title: moccasin
garment.reason: A beaded hide moccasin with floral beadwork design, attributed by the museum to Mohawk/Iroquois/Northeast Peoples makers—consistent with well-documented Haudenosaunee beadwork traditions.

arms.name: tomahawk pipe
arms.title: tomahawk pipe
arms.reason: A pipe tomahawk historically associated with and used by the Mohawk leader Joseph Brant (Thayendanegea), though physically manufactured in Sheffield, England for the Native trade — this is a documented object used by the named Mohawk figure, fitting the "used by" criterion even though made by outsiders for trade.
